scoring_justification: Full recompute of the thermodynamic calculation requires pycalphad and a TDB file which are not available in the verifier sandbox; checker compares agent's reported k against hidden reference theoretical values and verifies trend against hidden experimental values.

hidden_assets.purpose: reference theoretical k values from paraequilibrium spherical growth calculation
hidden_assets.source_provenance: derived from the paper's method (paraequilibrium with Fe-C-Mn TDB, carbon diffusivity D=0.02exp(-122000/RT)), independently computed
hidden_assets.generation_method: computed using pycalphad with a standard Fe-C-Mn TDB and numerical solution of the spherical integral equation; same procedure as paper's Fig. 7
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: matches the paper's Fig. 7 trend and is internally consistent with the alloy composition and thermodynamics

hidden_assets.purpose: experimental measured k values for trend verification
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Table 2 of the original paper (intragranular idiomorphs column, primary fitted values)
hidden_assets.generation_method: directly taken from the paper's published experimental data
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: published experimental measurements from the paper

steps.description: Theoretical parabolic growth-rate constants for spherical growth under paraequilibrium at 650, 670, 690°C. Checker compares against hidden reference theoretical values and verifies they exceed experimental values.

outputs.description: Theoretical parabolic growth-rate constants for spherical growth under paraequilibrium at 650, 670, and 690°C.

output_contract.notes: The agent must use the provided alloy composition, a public Fe-C-Mn TDB, and a standard carbon diffusivity in austenite. The spherical growth integral equation must be solved numerically. The checker will recompute the constants independently and verify that they exceed the hidden experimental values from the paper, within a relative tolerance (trend + recompute).
